full_judgment:
KM Hafizul Alam J : This Rule, at the instance of the petitioner, was issued under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (in short the Code) calling upon the opposite-party to show cause as to why the proceeding of Sutrapur Police Station Case No. 62 dated 29-1-2004, corresponding to ACC GR No. 4 of 2004 under sections 420/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860, now pending in the Court of Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No. 2, Dhaka should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Short facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of this Rule, are that one Md Moniruzzaman Khan, Anti-Corruption Officer, Anti-Corruption Bureau, Dhaka as informant lodged a First Information Report (in brief the FIR) Area, Dhaka with the Sutrapur Police Station being No. 62 dated 29-1-2008 under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860 against the accused-petitioner. The allegation inter alia was that at the time of inquiry of nothi No. 347-2000 the informant came to know that one Srimoti Trinoyni Das, wife of late Sudhir Chandra Das, 48 North Blockhall Road, Police Station-Sutrapur, District-Dhaka was the owner of 0.1140 acres of land in plot No. 1056 of SA Khatian No. 624 under Sutrapur Mouza, Dhaka. At the time of her death in the year 1972 she had no successor in Bangladesh. Therefore, the Government of Bangladesh became the owner of the said 0.1140 acres of land along with her all other properties. But after the death of the Srimoti Treenoney Das, Md Abul Kashem Howlader son of Abul Zalil Howlader created a forged sale deed being No. 1228 dated 28-6-1997. Thereafter he used the said deed before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kotwali Circle on 21-8-1991 a in Namjari Case No. 773(Su)/91-92. The accused Md Abul Kashem by using that deed got the residence No. 68-69, Paridash Road measuring 0.0400 acres of land mutated in his name. The accused thereby committed offence under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860. 

 3. The investigating officer after investigation the case submitted a charge-sheet being No. 471 dated 27-11-2011 under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860 against the petitioner before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 4. After submission of the charge-sheet the learned Magistrate was pleased to frame charge under sections 420/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860 against the accused-petitioner on 1-8-2012. 

 9. Mr Amin further submits that the informant has no locus-stadi to lodge the instant FIR as because sections 420/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860 is included in the schedule of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 on 20-11-2013 but the informant lodged the instant FIR on 29-1-2004 long before inclusion of the said sections in the said schedule moreover, the instant case has been investigated by the ACC Officer which is abuse of the process of law as such, the instant proceeding is liable to be quashed for the ends of justice. 

 13. Mr Khan, lastly submits that the instant proceeding is not barred by section 195 (1)(c) of the Penal Code, 1860 and the revenue officer is not required to proceed under section 476 of the Code as the revenue officer does not fall within the category of court as stated in section 195 (1)(c) of the Penal Code, 1860. 

 18. In this context, let us examine the first issue as to the legality of initiation of the case. In this regard the main submission of the petitioner is that as the alleged deed was used before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), the initiation of the case by any person other than Assistant Commissioner (Land) is barred by section 195(1)(c) of the Code. With regard to this issue our apex court in the case of Malik Fateh Khan vs Najibulla, reported in 9 DLR (WP) 40, Idrish Ali vs State, reported in 38 DLR 270, Chitta Ranjan Das vs Shashi Mohan Das, reported in 56 DLR 276 and in the case of Sahera Khatun vs Abdur Rahim Sk, reported in 13 BLC (AD) 24 consistently held that the Revenue Officer disposing of an application seeking mutation cannot be considered a Court and, as such, a case initiated on a private complaint for using alleged forged and fabricated papers in the mutation proceeding is not barred by the provision of the section 195(1)(c) of the Code since order of the Revenue Officer in either way disposing of the application seeking mutation is not an order of the Court. In view of the above decisions and provision of section 195(1)(c) we don't find any force in the submission of the petitioner that the initiation of the case is barred by law. 

 21. In this regard, Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, learned advocate, for the opposite party No. 2 has referred the case of Faridul Alam vs State, reported in 61 DLR (AD) 93 wherein it has been held:

 27. However, with regard to the second issue as to investigation and continuation of trial, it appears that one Mr Md Moniruzzaman Khan, the officer of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption lodged an FIR on 29-1-2004 under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860 against the accused-petitioner for misappropriation of the government property by creating forged document. Thereafter, the Bureau of Anit-Corruption started investigation of the said case. In the meantime, the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 (in short the ACC Act, 2004) came into force on 9-5-2004. The above mentioned sections 420/ 467/468/471 were not included in the schedule of the said ACC Act, 2004 but as the said sections were included in the schedule of Anti-Corruption Act, 1957, therefore the Bureau had authority to lodge FIR, as such, initiation of the case was not barred by law. After repealing of the Anti-Corruption Act, 1957 the Anti-Corruption Commission (in short the ACC) pursuant to the provision of section 38(3) of the ACC Act, 2004 continued to investigate the said case and accordingly submitted charge-sheet under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860 on 27-11-2011. Thereafter the learned Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No. 1, Dhaka vide order dated 1-8-2012 framed charge against the petitioner under sections 420/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860. The learned Magistrate also examined one prosecution witness. In the meantime, the schedule of the ACC Act, 2004 was amended on 20-11-2013 and sections 420/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860 were included in the said schedule. Subsequently the said schedule was further amended on 21-6-2016 and sections 420/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860 were made applicable for limited purpose specially so far as it relates to the government property is concerned.
